topics.topic: MCP listener validation, binding lifecycle, failure behavior, and cleanup
questions: When and how is the MCP listen address validated and bound, and what happens if binding or opening the entrance fails after recovery changes have committed?
At what point is the MCP listener bound, and what output/error results when binding or listening fails?
When is the listen address bound, and what output, error and cleanup apply if the address is invalid, unavailable or loses its listener during service?

quotes: serve_kernel: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST call run_start_sequence with config_path, the process's one command-line argument, and open the MCP entrance — MCP over streamable HTTP at the mcp_listen_address of the returned Installation, one tool per catalogue operation — only after it returned; while serving it reads one HTTP request at a time, takes the presented token from its Authorization header in the Bearer form (None when the header is absent or not in that form), passes the body bytes and that token to answer_request and writes back the bytes it returns.

serve_kernel: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns the process exit code: non-zero after a failed start, a required stop, or any internal_error that answer_request let propagate — in both of the last two cases the request is first answered internal_error without detail and then the process ends — zero only when serving ends normally.
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats an invalid or unavailable listen address, or later listener failure, as a fatal non-zero process exit that preserves committed recovery changes; another retries, keeps running without an entrance, or treats listener loss as normal termination. The owner, host supervisor, and MCP callers notice whether the kernel exits, retries, or remains unreachable.
judgement.why: The texts place opening after recovery but do not specify listen-address validation, bind/listen failure handling, retry policy, or listener-loss behavior.

topics.topic: Unit used to measure disclosed masked failure-detail length
questions: Is the disclosed failure-detail length counted in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, grapheme clusters, or another unit?
Is the disclosed length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another unit?
Is the disclosed length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another unit?

quotes: handle_get_repair_view: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] The class of a NodeExecution is the highest class among the items of its inputs, each SpooledFilesRef counting with its disclosure_class even when empty, and when its executed names a binding also of its outputs; the class of an operation execution's failure_detail is the highest of that class and the disclosure classes read_binding declares for that binding's outputs; the class of a TrialExecution is the highest class among its TrialCase's inputs (A07 rule 5, A09 rule 7); a failure_detail becomes DetailLength with its UTF-8 byte length and that class when the reader is an agent and the class is above open, and DetailText otherwise, always for the owner.
judgement.why: The later notes explicitly define the disclosed length as the UTF-8 byte length.

topics.topic: Startup manifest validation scope, checks, and ordering for credential-bearing services
questions: Which manifest checks must run at start for each credential-bearing service, and are unrelated capability entries validated?
Which exact manifest checks are applied at startup for each credential-bearing service, and in what order?

judgement.why: This is the same question about operation-independent startup manifest checks for credential-bearing services, already judged in P2 on unchanged later-state passages.

precedent.topic: Manifest checks applicable during startup without operation context
quotes: read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.

check_installed_instances: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Takes the services the installation holds a credential for, in service_id order by Unicode code point, and for each raises RefusedError naming that service at the first failure: first the credential header name equals a name in the imported KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES constant compared without regard to case, host included, checked without reading the manifest; then, only when the installation selects an instance for the service, its record read by read_service_record fails any check, or the selected instance named in the record has a required header whose name equals the credential header name compared without regard to case.

check_installed_instances: [BEHAVIOR] A service with no selected instance, or whose record lists no instance of the selected name, fails nothing here; the check reads only the given installation and the manifest, never the store, and returns None when every service passes.
precedent.why: The later notes restrict startup validation to operation-independent service-record checks and credential-header collisions for selected instances.
